Patient Billing & Cash Collection Policy

Document ID: ANGH-07_ | Department: 03_Finance_and_Billing

Version: 2.1 | Effective Date: 01 September 2026 | Review Date: 01 September 2027

Owner: Hospital Operations & Quality Directorate | Classification: Internal

Purpose

Defines charging, invoice generation, payment collection, refunds, discounts, and financial reconciliation.

Billing Workflow

Clinical services and consumables are captured from approved source systems.

Billing staff validate charges before invoice finalization.

Patient receives an itemized invoice where applicable.

Cashier records payment against the correct patient account and payment method.

Refunds and Adjustments

Refunds, write-offs, and manual adjustments require documented authorization according to the financial delegation matrix.

Daily Reconciliation

Refunds, write-offs, and manual adjustments require documented authorization according to the financial delegation matrix.

Daily Reconciliation

Cash, card, bank transfer, and approved digital payment records are reconciled against system transactions at the end of each business day.

KPIs

Billing accuracy ≥98.5%. Daily cash reconciliation completion = 100%. Unresolved billing exceptions older than 7 days should remain below 2%.

Governance

All departments follow the Hospital Policy Governance Standard. Exceptions require documented approval from the responsible director and Quality Directorate.

Escalation Matrix

Operational issues are escalated first to the department supervisor, then department head, and finally the relevant executive or on-call leader depending on severity.

Purpose

Standardizes insurance eligibility, pre-authorization, claim preparation, submission, rejection handling, and reconciliation.

Eligibility

Insurance desk verifies policy status, member details, coverage limits, exclusions, and required referral/pre-authorization.

Pre-Authorization

Collect clinical justification and required reports.

Submit authorization through the insurer's approved channel.

Track authorization number, approved services, validity period, and financial limits.

Escalate delayed approvals that may affect patient care.

Claims

Escalate delayed approvals that may affect patient care.

Claims

Claims include patient identifiers, service codes, clinical documentation, approved authorization, invoices, and required attachments.

KPIs

Clean-claim rate ≥95%. Pre-authorization turnaround for standard requests ≤4 hours. Claims rejection rate target <5%.

Governance

All departments follow the Hospital Policy Governance Standard. Exceptions require documented approval from the responsible director and Quality Directorate.

Laboratory Specimen Collection & Reporting SOP

Document ID: ANGH-05_ | Department: 02_Pharmacy_and_Laboratory

Version: 2.1 | Effective Date: 01 September 2026 | Review Date: 01 September 2027

Owner: Hospital Operations & Quality Directorate | Classification: Internal

Purpose

Ensures specimen identification, collection, transport, analysis, result validation, and reporting are controlled.

Specimen Collection

Verify patient using two identifiers.

Label specimen immediately at the collection point.

Record collection time and collector identity.

Reject specimens that are unlabeled, mismatched, leaking, or unsuitable for the requested test.

Critical Results

Critical laboratory results are communicated to the responsible clinical team immediately and read-back is documented.

Turnaround Times

Critical laboratory results are communicated to the responsible clinical team immediately and read-back is documented.

Turnaround Times

Routine CBC target: ≤90 minutes. Routine chemistry target: ≤120 minutes. Urgent tests follow department-specific escalation targets.

Quality Controls

Daily internal quality controls are reviewed before releasing affected analytical results. External quality assessment participation is maintained for applicable tests.

Governance

All departments follow the Hospital Policy Governance Standard. Exceptions require documented approval from the responsible director and Quality Directorate.

Escalation Matrix

Operational issues are escalated first to the department supervisor, then department head, and finally the relevant executive or on-call leader depending on severity.

Blood Bank Operations & Transfusion Policy

Document ID: ANGH-06_ | Department: 02_Pharmacy_and_Laboratory

Version: 2.1 | Effective Date: 01 September 2026 | Review Date: 01 September 2027

Owner: Hospital Operations & Quality Directorate | Classification: Internal

Purpose

Defines safe blood request, compatibility testing, storage, issue, bedside verification, administration, reaction management, and traceability.

Blood Request

The authorized clinician documents indication, component type, quantity, urgency, and relevant clinical information.

Compatibility and Issue

Patient identification and sample labelling are verified before testing.

Blood components are issued only against an authorized request.

Temperature-controlled storage is monitored continuously or through approved validated monitoring systems.

Bedside Verification

Temperature-controlled storage is monitored continuously or through approved validated monitoring systems.

Bedside Verification

Two qualified staff verify patient identity, blood group, component type, unit number, expiry, and compatibility documentation before transfusion.

Transfusion Reaction

Stop transfusion immediately if a reaction is suspected, maintain IV access with appropriate fluid, notify the physician and blood bank, and document the event according to incident-reporting procedures.

Governance

All departments follow the Hospital Policy Governance Standard. Exceptions require documented approval from the responsible director and Quality Directorate.

Escalation Matrix

Operational issues are escalated first to the department supervisor, then department head, and finally the relevant executive or on-call leader depending on severity.

Pharmacy Dispensing & Medication Management

Document ID: ANGH-04_ | Department: 02_Pharmacy_and_Laboratory

Version: 2.1 | Effective Date: 01 September 2026 | Review Date: 01 September 2027

Owner: Hospital Operations & Quality Directorate | Classification: Internal

Purpose

Controls medication procurement, storage, prescribing review, dispensing, administration support, and medication reconciliation.

Dispensing Workflow

Prescription received → pharmacist clinical review → stock verification → dispensing → independent check → patient/ward handover → transaction recording.

Controlled medicines require authorized prescription and register entry.

Storage

Refrigerated medicines are maintained at 2–8°C unless manufacturer instructions specify otherwise. Temperature excursions are documented and escalated.

Medication Reconciliation

Medication Reconciliation

Pharmacy compares home medicines, admission orders, transfers, and discharge prescriptions to identify omissions, duplication, interactions, and dose discrepancies.

KPIs

Dispensing accuracy ≥99.5%. Refrigerator temperature compliance ≥99%. Medication reconciliation completion for eligible admissions ≥95%.

Governance

All departments follow the Hospital Policy Governance Standard. Exceptions require documented approval from the responsible director and Quality Directorate.

Escalation Matrix

Operational issues are escalated first to the department supervisor, then department head, and finally the relevant executive or on-call leader depending on severity.

Inpatient Nursing Operations SOP

Document ID: ANGH-03_ | Department: 01_Clinical_Operations

Version: 2.1 | Effective Date: 01 September 2026 | Review Date: 01 September 2027

Owner: Hospital Operations & Quality Directorate | Classification: Internal

Purpose

Defines core nursing routines for safe inpatient care.

Shift Handover

Use SBAR: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation.

Confirm patient identity, current diagnosis, allergies, lines/tubes, medications, pending investigations, fall risk, and outstanding clinical concerns.

Medication Safety

Use two patient identifiers before medication administration.

Check medication, dose, route, timing, allergies, and documented indication.

High-alert medications require independent verification according to the medication safety list.

Hourly Rounding

High-alert medications require independent verification according to the medication safety list.

Hourly Rounding

Nurses assess pain, position, personal needs, environment, and safety risks at defined intervals. Significant changes are documented in the EHR.

KPIs

Medication administration documentation compliance ≥98%. Nursing handover compliance ≥95%. Fall incidents are reviewed through the patient-safety process.

Governance

All departments follow the Hospital Policy Governance Standard. Exceptions require documented approval from the responsible director and Quality Directorate.

Escalation Matrix

Operational issues are escalated first to the department supervisor, then department head, and finally the relevant executive or on-call leader depending on severity.

Patient Admission & Discharge Policy

Document ID: ANGH-01_ | Department: 01_Clinical_Operations

Version: 2.1 | Effective Date: 01 September 2026 | Review Date: 01 September 2027

Owner: Hospital Operations & Quality Directorate | Classification: Internal

Purpose

Defines the standard process for elective and emergency admission, patient identification, bed allocation, transfer, discharge planning, and post-discharge documentation.

Admission Process

Registration verifies patient identity using two identifiers.

The admitting clinician records diagnosis, clinical priority, allergies, medication history, and required level of care.

Bed Management assigns an appropriate bed based on acuity, isolation status, gender, and specialty.

Nursing completes the initial assessment within 30 minutes of arrival to the ward.

Discharge Process

Nursing completes the initial assessment within 30 minutes of arrival to the ward.

Discharge Process

The responsible clinician confirms clinical readiness and discharge orders.

Pharmacy reconciles discharge medications and provides counselling when required.

Billing confirms financial clearance or approved credit/insurance arrangements.

The patient receives a discharge summary, medication instructions, follow-up appointment, and emergency contact guidance.

KPIs

Admission registration accuracy target: 99%. Discharge summary completion before departure target: 98%. Average discharge processing time target: below 45 minutes.

Governance

All departments follow the Hospital Policy Governance Standard. Exceptions require documented approval from the responsible director and Quality Directorate.

Escalation Matrix

Operational issues are escalated first to the department supervisor, then department head, and finally the relevant executive or on-call leader depending on severity.

Emergency Department Operations SOP

Document ID: ANGH-02_ | Department: 01_Clinical_Operations

Version: 2.1 | Effective Date: 01 September 2026 | Review Date: 01 September 2027

Owner: Hospital Operations & Quality Directorate | Classification: Internal

Purpose

Standardizes triage, emergency assessment, stabilization, referral, observation, admission, and discharge.

Triage

A registered nurse assigns triage priority using the hospital's five-level acuity model. Immediate threats to airway, breathing, circulation, consciousness, or severe bleeding receive the highest priority.

Clinical Workflow

Triage → registration → clinician assessment → diagnostics/treatment → reassessment → disposition.

Critical patients are transferred directly to the resuscitation area.

Patients requiring admission are handed over using a structured clinical handoff.

Escalation

Patients requiring admission are handed over using a structured clinical handoff.

Escalation

Any deterioration, abnormal critical result, suspected sepsis, major trauma, or unmanageable workload must be escalated to the ED consultant and nursing supervisor.

KPIs

Door-to-triage target: ≤10 minutes. Door-to-provider target for high-acuity cases: ≤15 minutes. Left-without-being-seen target: <2%.

Governance

All departments follow the Hospital Policy Governance Standard. Exceptions require documented approval from the responsible director and Quality Directorate.

Escalation Matrix

Operational issues are escalated first to the department supervisor, then department head, and finally the relevant executive or on-call leader depending on severity.

Version: 2.1 | Effective Date: 01 September 2026 | Review Date: 01 September 2027

Owner: Hospital Operations & Quality Directorate | Classification: Internal

Purpose

Defines preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, biomedical equipment control, utilities monitoring, and work-order management.

Work Orders

Staff submit maintenance requests through the facilities system.

Requests are classified as emergency, urgent, or routine.

Emergency failures affecting patient safety or critical utilities receive immediate escalation.

Preventive Maintenance

Maintenance schedules are maintained for generators, HVAC, medical gas systems, lifts, fire systems, and biomedical equipment.

Biomedical Equipment

Maintenance schedules are maintained for generators, HVAC, medical gas systems, lifts, fire systems, and biomedical equipment.

Biomedical Equipment

Equipment is tagged with asset ID, location, service status, calibration requirements, and maintenance history. Failed equipment is removed from clinical use until cleared.

KPIs

Critical equipment preventive-maintenance completion ≥95%. Emergency work-order response target ≤15 minutes.

Governance

All departments follow the Hospital Policy Governance Standard. Exceptions require documented approval from the responsible director and Quality Directorate.

Operational issues are escalated first to the department supervisor, then department head, and finally the relevant executive or on-call leader depending on severity.

Owner: Hospital Operations & Quality Directorate | Classification: Internal

Purpose

Controls demand planning, requisition, sourcing, purchase orders, receiving, inspection, storage, and supplier performance.

Procurement Workflow

Department raises approved requisition.

Procurement obtains quotations or uses an approved contract.

Authorized approver confirms purchase order.

Stores verifies quantity, condition, batch/expiry, and delivery documentation.

Invoice is matched against purchase order and receipt.

Medical Supplies

Critical items such as PPE, IV sets, syringes, and emergency medicines are maintained at defined minimum stock levels.

Supplier Management

Critical items such as PPE, IV sets, syringes, and emergency medicines are maintained at defined minimum stock levels.

Supplier Management

Suppliers are reviewed for quality, delivery performance, responsiveness, documentation, and regulatory compliance.

KPIs

Stock-out incidents for critical items <1% of requisition days. Purchase-order cycle time target ≤7 working days for standard purchases.

Governance

All departments follow the Hospital Policy Governance Standard. Exceptions require documented approval from the responsible director and Quality Directorate.

Infection Prevention & Control Manual

Document ID: ANGH-16_ | Department: 07_Quality_and_Compliance

Version: 2.1 | Effective Date: 01 September 2026 | Review Date: 01 September 2027

Owner: Hospital Operations & Quality Directorate | Classification: Internal

Purpose

Defines standard precautions, transmission-based precautions, hand hygiene, environmental cleaning, PPE, isolation, and surveillance.

Hand Hygiene

Staff perform hand hygiene before patient contact, before aseptic tasks, after body-fluid exposure risk, after patient contact, and after contact with patient surroundings.

Isolation

Patients requiring contact, droplet, airborne, or protective precautions are identified promptly and managed according to the relevant isolation procedure.

Environmental Cleaning

High-touch surfaces are cleaned at defined frequencies. Cleaning deviations are documented and corrected.

Surveillance

Environmental Cleaning

High-touch surfaces are cleaned at defined frequencies. Cleaning deviations are documented and corrected.

Surveillance

Infection Prevention reviews healthcare-associated infection indicators, clusters, and trends and reports material findings to the Infection Control Committee.

Governance

All departments follow the Hospital Policy Governance Standard. Exceptions require documented approval from the responsible director and Quality Directorate.

Incident Reporting & Patient Safety Policy

Document ID: ANGH-15_ | Department: 07_Quality_and_Compliance

Version: 2.1 | Effective Date: 01 September 2026 | Review Date: 01 September 2027

Owner: Hospital Operations & Quality Directorate | Classification: Internal

Purpose

Creates a non-punitive mechanism for reporting safety incidents, near misses, adverse events, and hazards.

Reportable Events

Medication errors and near misses.

Patient falls.

Wrong-patient or wrong-site events.

Equipment-related incidents.

Infection-control breaches.

Patient identification failures.

Reporting Workflow

Reporter submits event → supervisor ensures immediate safety actions → Quality team triages severity → investigation/root-cause analysis where required → corrective actions → closure and learning.

Escalation

Escalation

Serious harm, sentinel events, or events with potential regulatory significance are escalated immediately to senior leadership and relevant governance committees.

KPIs

Serious incidents escalated within defined SLA = 100%. Corrective-action closure within target ≥90%.

Governance

All departments follow the Hospital Policy Governance Standard. Exceptions require documented approval from the responsible director and Quality Directorate.

Escalation Matrix

Operational issues are escalated first to the department supervisor, then department head, and finally the relevant executive or on-call leader depending on severity.

Provides a common framework for performance goals, competency assessment, mandatory training, coaching, and annual review.

Goal setting at the beginning of the cycle.

Quarterly check-ins covering outcomes, behaviors, development needs, and risks.

Mid-year review and corrective development planning where required.

Annual performance review and development plan.

Mandatory Training

Clinical staff complete required patient-safety, infection-control, emergency response, and role-specific competency training. Non-clinical staff complete information security, privacy, workplace safety, and relevant compliance training.

Competency

High-risk clinical roles require documented competency validation before independent practice.

KPIs

Mandatory training completion ≥98%. Annual performance review completion ≥95%.

Governance

Hiring manager submits approved requisition.

HR screens candidates against role requirements.

New employees complete identity verification, employment documentation, mandatory orientation, infection-control training, information-security training, and department induction.

Leave

Employees submit leave through the HR system. Department managers assess operational coverage before approval. Emergency leave is recorded retrospectively when permitted by policy.

Records

Personnel records are restricted to authorized HR personnel and retained according to the hospital records-retention schedule.

Version: 2.1 | Effective Date: 01 September 2026 | Review Date: 01 September 2027

Owner: Hospital Operations & Quality Directorate | Classification: Internal

Purpose

Defines governance for electronic health records, data quality, privacy, access, retention, disclosure, and secondary use.

Data Quality

Patient demographic data should be complete and accurate.

Duplicate patient records are investigated and merged through an approved process.

Clinical corrections preserve an auditable history.

Privacy

Access to patient information is limited to legitimate care, operational, legal, or approved analytical purposes. Staff must not access records out of curiosity or without a business need.

Data Disclosure

Data Disclosure

External disclosures require appropriate authorization and documentation, subject to applicable law and hospital policy.

Retention and Audit

Records are retained according to the approved schedule. Access logs are reviewed for anomalous or unauthorized activity.

Governance

All departments follow the Hospital Policy Governance Standard. Exceptions require documented approval from the responsible director and Quality Directorate.

Protects hospital systems, endpoints, networks, applications, and user accounts from unauthorized access and cyber threats.

Access Management

Access is granted based on job role and least privilege.

Joiner, mover, and leaver events are processed through approved workflows.

Privileged access requires enhanced controls and periodic review.

Security Controls

Multi-factor authentication is required for designated systems. Passwords and credentials must not be shared. Suspected phishing, malware, or unauthorized access must be reported immediately.

Incident Response

IT Security records, triages, contains, investigates, and closes security incidents. High-severity incidents are escalated to the CIO and designated incident-response team.

KPIs

Leaver access removal within defined SLA ≥99%. Privileged-access review completion = 100%.

All departments follow the Hospital Policy Governance Standard. Exceptions require documented approval from the responsible director and Quality Directorate.
